To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) daily positive mood is associated with attention to rewarding information, (b) mood manipulations increase attention to rewarding information (vs. neutral information), and (c) mood manipulations do not increase attention to neutral information (vs. rewarding information).
positive mood states are associated with selective attention to rewarding stimuli, and this association is specific to positive stimuli and to positive mood states.
